text: A `catch` block that adds the line number and file name and rethrows fixes nothing. Why is it legitimate?
choices: It resets the stack trace, removing irrelevant library frames.
It converts a checked exception to unchecked, which callers prefer.
It adds information that exists only at that point, which can be the difference between an hour of debugging and a minute.
It is the only way to guarantee the exception reaches the top of `main`.
explanation: The rule is catch to add context, or catch to act — never catch to be seen catching. An operator reading `NumberFormatException: For input string: "N/A"` and one reading `line 4,127 of customers.csv, caused by ...` are in very different positions, and the second cost one line. Passing the cause is what makes it work; omitting it destroys what you were trying to preserve.
